cases.name: Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.
UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc.

profile_text.body:
Suno is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its site presents it as an AI music generator that turns a text prompt into a complete song with vocals, lyrics, and production in under a minute, and it also offers Suno Studio, which it describes as a first-of-its-kind web-based generative audio workstation combining traditional DAW functionality with AI-powered music creation. The site says the Pro plan includes 500 songs a month, access to v5.5, commercial use rights, priority generation, the Song Editor, stem separation, and audio uploads of up to 8 minutes, while the Premier plan adds 2,000 songs a month, Suno Studio, a multitrack editor, MIDI export, Persona Voices, and early access to new features.

The company describes itself on its site as the market-leading AI song generator and the number one AI music generator, and says millions of people already use it to make music. It positions the product against other AI music tools that it says produce short instrumental loops, claiming its own output spans full songs across every genre.

Suno's tracked litigation is substantial. Cases include Gawronski v. Suno Inc. in the District Court, S.D. Texas; Rugnetta v. Suno, Inc., Pilavian v. Suno, Inc., Reyna v. Suno, Inc., and S.A. Jamendo v. Suno Inc. in the District Court, D. Massachusetts; Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc. in the District Court, S.D. New York; Woulard v. Suno, Inc. in the District Court, N.D. Illinois; and UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc. in the U.S. District Court, D. Massachusetts. Massachusetts carries the largest share of that exposure, at 187. Suno's product listing notes music generation with IP provenance relevant.
